semantics: EVAP baseline-difference scaling helper. It subtracts two zero-extended uint16 arguments, multiplies the signed difference by ROM8[00008999]=112, arithmetic-shifts right by five, and upper-saturates the result at 65535.
contract: Given r4=a and r5=b, returns r0=min(65535, floor((uint16(a)-uint16(b))*112/32)) as a signed 32-bit result. Negative results are not lower-clamped.
note: EVAP producer paths pass captured baseline ffff2abc as a and current sample ffff10c4 as b, then clamp negative returns to zero before storing ffff2c92. The physical pressure scale of either sample remains unresolved.

semantics: EVAP negative-pressure leak transform. It maps baseline-relative coordinate ffff2c92 through 000152d6 into ffff3240, compares that result with the caller-supplied lookup at corrected coordinate ffff2c98, and writes zero when the transformed difference is nonpositive. A positive difference is normalized with caller parameter ffff2c86 and saturated into ffff3018. The final output is sat_u16(uint8[ffff2f8d] * uint16[ffff3018] * uint8[ffff2f94] >> 14).
note: Caller 000b29b8 supplies the second 000152d6 lookup result in r5, ffff2c86 in r4, and output pointer ffff301c in r6. The arithmetic and saturation are exact. Physical pressure conversion and the factory Service 06 leak-area publication conversion are not connected to this internal result by code.

semantics: First-channel override and upper-bound coordinator. On the admitted path it copies ffff2698 to ffff3026 and can clear ffff41f3.bit0. Fallback paths select ffff2a6a, zero, or ROM16[000092ec] for ffff3026 and set the override bit. It writes ffff3024 as 1000 when both service gates pass or ROM16[000092ea]=150 otherwise.
note: FUN 0007a592 consumes ffff3024 as its final upper bound and ffff3026 as its bit-gated override source. The physical quantity of these words is unresolved.

semantics: Second-channel override coordinator. The admitted path copies ffff277c to ffff35ea. Fallback paths select zero or ROM16[000162fe]=43. The function sets or clears ffff4214.bit6 so FUN 0007a804 and FUN 0007b0a0 select the override source consistently.
note: The gate conditions and source-selection mechanism are exact. The physical quantity of ffff277c and ffff35ea is unresolved.

semantics: Producer of common Q15 coefficient ffff31e2 for the two raw-output channels. It adjusts state ffff31e6 by ROM16[000093b8], bounds the state, looks up upper limit 00014fa2 on axis 00014f82 with input ffff2698, and writes max(0x8000, min(ffff31e6, lookup)) to ffff31e2.
note: All cells of 00014fa2 equal 0x8000 in stock JK08A, so the published coefficient is unity. FUN 0007a592 and FUN 0007a804 apply it with a right shift of 15. The physical purpose of the coefficient is unresolved.

semantics: Cross-channel disagreement monitor for final words ffff2a7a and ffff35cc. Under four entry gates it calculates abs(uint16(ffff2a7a)-uint16(ffff35cc)), writes the result to ffff2c1c, and when the difference exceeds 26 invokes service dispatcher 0007d8b8 with argument 0x62 after a local countdown permits it.
note: This proves that the two crossfade components are parallel calculation channels whose final raw outputs are checked for agreement. It does not identify their physical quantity.

semantics: ATU-II channel 3 periodic interrupt handler and scheduler-flag producer. Every invocation advances GR3A by 0x140 timer counts and sets ffff84b9 bit 7; a modulo-4 phase sets bit 6 every second invocation and bit 5 every fourth, while a modulo-10 phase sets bits 4 and 2 every tenth. On the tenth phase it decrements every nonzero byte in ffff256a..ffff25f3, including DFCO timers ffff2571..ffff2573 and stationary-limiter timer ffff258a, then calls FUN 000209d8 and returns with RTE. It also ORs 0x80 into tick-flag byte ffff84c4 at 00020734, which scheduler 00020dfe snapshots into ffff84c3 on every pass.
note: Normal initialization sets PSCR1=1 and TCR3=5, giving timer input Pphi/64. The base period is exactly 20480/Pphi seconds and the tenth-phase byte-timer period is 204800/Pphi. Passive target-CAN timestamps establish Pphi=20 MHz and 10.24 ms per count.

semantics: Engine-event scheduler feeder and timing-task dispatcher. It first calls 00028af8 and 00028b5c to publish two wrap-corrected interval snapshots, then sets ffff84ba bit 7, advances modulo-3 phase ffff9f24, and sets ffff84ba bit 6 when the phase reaches three. It invokes all ten entries of the engine-event task table at 00021b5c; index 4 is timing dispatcher 0004e162.
note: Three admitted current-cylinder events correspond to one crankshaft revolution on the V6. The table order establishes that final timing-coordinate construction and APC scheduling execute in the engine-event path.

semantics: Pending-task dispatcher called by periodic interrupt handler 0002040c. It drains bit-selected function tables. When ffff84b9 bit 5 is set, it invokes all seven entries at 00021818; FUN 0003a904 is index 2 and Base Fuel Schedule producer FUN 0003b75c is index 3. After the table, it copies 24 bytes ffff1dec..ffff1e03 to ffff1e04..ffff1e1b. It also copies the eight-byte current RPM-drop filter block ffff1e50..ffff1e57 to preceding-snapshot block ffff1e58..ffff1e5f. When ffff84ba bit 6 is set, it invokes all three entries at 00021960, including FUN 0007c494 at index 1.
note: Periodic handler 0002040c sets ffff84b9 bit 5 every fourth base interrupt. The engine-event phase separately produces ffff84ba bit 6 every third admitted current-cylinder event; dispatcher delay does not change either relative divisor under normal pending-flag service.

semantics: Primary startup RAM initializer driven by descriptor table 0x225F4. Its second longword loop clears effective span [ffff261c,ffff4514), whose unaligned descriptor stop is ffff4512; this span includes AN1-path phase mask ffff3f3e, first-sample mask ffff3f44, running-min accumulator ffff3f4c, shared fuel-inhibit prerequisite byte ffff418c, diagnostic status byte ffff41ea, P030 status byte ffff41d2, selector byte ffff422d, and inter-cycle latch ffff42a8. It later invokes secondary initializer FUN 00027c50.
note: Startup entry FUN 00027e24 calls this initializer at 00027ebc before the main loop. Longword stores through ffff4510 prove zero initialization of the complete listed state.

semantics: Startup RAM initializer driven by descriptor table 0x2260C. Its longword loops clear [ffff84a0,ffff981c) and effective span [ffff1000,ffff261c), whose unaligned descriptor stop is ffff261a; the latter includes fallback bytes ffff107e..ffff1080 and fuel-inhibit prerequisite byte ffff2494. It also copies initialized data from ROM 0x25590 to RAM [ffff9f0c,ffffa314) before invoking two completion helpers.
note: Startup entry FUN 00027e24 reaches this initializer before the main loop; the descriptor endpoints and longword width prove zero initialization of the listed state.

semantics: Conditional RAM-clear service. When ffff2451 bit 5 is clear, descriptor table 0x2260C drives longword clears of [ffff84a0,ffffa314) and effective span [ffff1000,ffff5cf4), whose unaligned descriptor stop is ffff5cf2; the latter includes fallback bytes ffff107e..ffff1080, fuel-inhibit prerequisite bytes ffff2494 and ffff418c, diagnostic status byte ffff41ea, and AN1-path state ffff3f3e, ffff3f44, and ffff3f4c. Peripheral-state service calls follow the clears. The set-bit branch skips them.
note: FUN 0002f888 reaches this service from command/state branches. The exact clear spans are proven; the external meaning of those branches is not assigned.

semantics: Recovery loop and conditional RAM initializer. One entry-state branch uses descriptor table 0x225F4 to clear [ffff84a0,ffffa314) and effective span [ffff1000,ffff5cf4), whose unaligned descriptor stop is ffff5cf2; the latter includes fallback bytes ffff107e..ffff1080, fuel-inhibit prerequisite bytes ffff2494 and ffff418c, diagnostic status byte ffff41ea, and AN1-path state ffff3f3e, ffff3f44, and ffff3f4c. The function then continues its non-returning service loop.
note: The exact clear spans and non-returning loop are code-proven. The physical cause represented by the entry-state condition remains unresolved.

semantics: Saturated engine-speed byte producer. FUN 000384fe first writes ffff11e8 = ffff1196 >> 3; this function writes ffff11ea = min(255, ffff11e8 >> 3), therefore min(255, ffff1196 >> 6). It also maintains two prior samples at ffff229a/ffff229b and sets ffff2219 when the selected three-sample sequence is strictly increasing.
note: The output has the same RPM/12.5 count scale as word ffff11f4, which FUN 000384fe forms directly as ffff1196 >> 6. The byte saturates at 255.

semantics: Engine-event frequency scaler. When ffff417f bit 5 is clear, it writes ffff1206=floor(ROM8[0x88fb]*uint32[ffff22d4]/12000000) and ffff1208=floor(ffff1206/2); when the bit is set, it writes zero to both words.
note: ROM8[0x88fb] is 3 in all six project ROMs, matching the number of intake events per crankshaft revolution for a four-stroke V6. Code proves the event-count arithmetic; the physical source and timebase of ffff22d4 remain unresolved.

semantics: Rotational-reference interval history updater. When ffff84f2 bit 7 announces a sample, it clears that pending bit, sets ffff84f8 bit 7, and requires speed-qualification counter ffff4096 to reach stock ROM8[000083b8] = 1 plus prior-reference latch ffff84f1 bit 7. A valid sample shifts the 14-longword interval history rooted at ffff1dac and updates three saturating sample-age counters. Counter ffff3834 increments only while ffff4247 bit 6 is set; otherwise it resets. An invalid sample fills the history with the current interval and resets all three counters.
note: Detection core 00085a70 requires ffff3834 >= 19; revolution-window producer 000872d0 requires >= 31. The counter unit is accepted intervals between consecutive selector-9 ICR0A captures. Static code does not establish captures per crankshaft revolution or unit time, or the initialization source of ffff4247 bit 6.

semantics: Periodic diagnostic dispatcher invoked as entry 100 of the 124-function table in scheduler 00020dfe. In one pass it invokes diagnostic group-summary builder 00097eb4, misfire coordinator 00082c8a, and cleanup helper 00085a1c; its recovered tail at 0007c166 recomputes the critical ECM/ETC aggregate in ffff41ea.bit5.
note: This establishes the coordinator service path; the base scheduler frequency remains unnamed.

semantics: Fast periodic misfire dispatcher. It is entry 12 of the 14-function ffff84b9-bit-6 table, which runs every second base periodic interrupt, and calls detection core 00085a70 between helpers 0003cf24 and 0008286a.
note: The relative divisor is exact; the physical interrupt period is unresolved.

semantics: Revolution-phase misfire dispatcher. It is entry 1 of the three-function ffff84ba-bit-6 table. Each service calls FUN 0007c4e0 and then tail-calls revolution-window producer 000872d0.
note: The pending flag is produced every third admitted current-cylinder event, corresponding to one crankshaft revolution on the V6.

semantics: Per-revolution engine-speed qualification updater for the misfire monitor. It applies hysteresis to saturated RPM/12.5 byte ffff11b2 through ffff24c4 bit 7: a clear state sets at stock ROM8[00008bda] = 32, while an already-set state adds four before comparison and therefore remains set at 28 or above. While the state is set it increments saturating byte ffff4096; while clear it resets the counter to zero.
note: The RPM/12.5 scale makes the set threshold 400 RPM and the retained-state lower boundary 350 RPM. The caller cadence is once per crankshaft revolution.

semantics: Periodic scheduler and snapshot copier reached from the main loop when ffff84b9 bit 2 is pending; handler 0002040c sets that bit every tenth base interrupt. It moves current Base Fuel Schedule ffff1024 to previous sample ffff1028 and then copies newest producer word ffff1026 to ffff1024. It calls block copier 00022104 with source ffff1048, destination ffff102c, and length 0x1c, establishing the internal normalized-BFS load snapshot ffff1048 -> ffff102c. It copies ffff1072..ffff1079 to ffff106a..ffff1071, establishing ffff1076 -> ffff106e for selected raw temperature, ffff1077 -> ffff106f for normalized coolant, ffff1078 -> ffff1070 for selected normalized temperature, and ffff1079 -> ffff1071 for raw coolant. It also copies ffff1114..ffff1193 to ffff1094..ffff1113 and ffff11d4..ffff120b to ffff119c..ffff11d3, establishing ffff1188 -> ffff1108 for battery voltage, ffff118e -> ffff110e for coarse vehicle speed, ffff11e6 -> ffff11ae for RPM/50, ffff11ea -> ffff11b2 for saturated RPM/12.5, ffff11eb -> ffff11b3 for RPM/25, and ffff11f4 -> ffff11bc for the RPM/12.5 word, ffff1200 -> ffff11c8 and ffff1201 -> ffff11c9 for the exhaust-cam edge phase bytes. It copies ffff120e..ffff124b to ffff124c..ffff1289 through FUN 00022558, establishing ffff1246 -> ffff1284 for the exhaust-VTC bank-enable snapshot. A 0x104-byte call to FUN 00022558 copies ffff277e..ffff2881 to ffff267a..ffff277d, including ffff283a -> ffff2736 and ffff2876 -> ffff2772 for the oil-temperature snapshot. It copies ffff2451/ffff2452 to ffff244f/ffff2450, shifts ffff2458 to previous snapshot ffff245a, copies producer ffff2459 to current snapshot ffff2458, and copies ffff246a..ffff246f to prior-cycle state. It copies tick-flag byte ffff84c4 to ffff84c3 at 00020ee6 and reloads ffff84c4 from ffff84bb at 00020ef0, copies ffff2324..ffff2329 to ffff231e..ffff2323 at 00021308 and to ffff232a..ffff232f at 00021310, and copies ffff4124..ffff417b to ffff40cc..ffff4123 at 0002132c, establishing ffff4178 -> ffff4120 and ffff4179 -> ffff4121 for the edge-count arm bytes. A 0x8c-byte call to FUN 00022558 at 00021314 copies ffff23bc..ffff2447 to ffff2330..ffff23bb, establishing ffff23d4 -> ffff2348 for the transformed injection-pulse array, ffff241c -> ffff2390 for the minimum pulse, and ffff2436 -> ffff23aa for the injector opening time.
note: The copy directions, lengths, exact offsets, and every-tenth-interrupt cadence are code-proven. The ffff1048 block copy runs before periodic tasks produce the next ffff1026 and ffff1048 values, so ffff102c is the coordinate consumed during the current pass. Exact DID 0x1103 identifies ffff1188 as battery voltage. Normal timer initialization makes this scheduler cadence exactly 204800/Pphi seconds; passive target-CAN timestamps establish Pphi=20 MHz and 10.24 ms per pass.

contract: Not arithmetic: ROM self-test initializer. It takes no arguments, and no register is read before being written. Its only effect is *(u32)0xFFFF2C04 = 0x00008204, which places the background scan cursor at the start of the monitored region. It returns no result and clobbers r0, r2, and r6.

Not arithmetic: background ROM self-test scanner initializer. It takes no arguments. It writes two words: cursor 0xFFFF2FF4 = 0x0002040C and scan step 0xFFFF3004 = 478 = (end - start) / 18 + 1, using unsigned division through call 00021ce0. It returns no result.

Not arithmetic: incremental ROM self-test scanner. It takes no arguments. Each call scans the next group of longwords from cursor 0xFFFF2FF4, accumulates XOR in 0xFFFF3000 and a sum in 0xFFFF3008, and advances the cursor. It returns no result: r0 contains garbage at both rts instructions, while r12-r14 and PR are preserved. Execution is gated by bit 7 of 0xFFFF4184.

Not arithmetic: ROM self-test verifier. It takes no arguments. It compares accumulators 0xFFFF3000 (XOR) and 0xFFFF3008 (sum) with ROM references [0x00020408] = 0x07131670 and [0x00020404] = 0xAC399870. A match has no side effects. On mismatch under interrupt mask IMASK = 15 it clears bit 12 in the 16-bit peripheral register 0xFFFFF74E and calls 0007d8b8 with fault code 0x75 in r4.

Not arithmetic: ROM self-test pass epilogue. It takes no arguments and runs unconditionally after every completed pass. It performs four writes: 0xFFFF2B1C <- 0xFFFF3000 (XOR latch), 0xFFFF2B20 <- 0xFFFF3008 (sum latch), then clears both accumulators for the next pass. It returns no result and has no diagnostic channel.

Not arithmetic: default exception and interrupt handler. It takes no arguments, and every register touched by the body is written before it is read. It sets SP = 0xFFFF7FFC and VBR = 0x00020004, then jumps to 00027e24 for reinitialization; it does not return or produce a result. It is addressed only through the vector table, in 222 of 256 slots. The body extends through 0x21bb0 inclusive; Ghidra's declared size of 20 stops one instruction early.

Signed 32/32 division: r0 = r1 / r0 (dividend r1, divisor r0), truncating toward zero (-7/2 = -3). It does not return a remainder. It clobbers r1; r2, r3, and r4 are preserved on the stack. Division-by-zero diagnostic: when r0 == 0, it writes 0x0000044E to 0xFFFF9818 and returns 0 without raising a trap, so the caller cannot distinguish failure from a valid zero by the return value.

semantics: Unsigned 32/32 division, a shared library primitive. In two analyzed components it closes a fixed-point denominator: angle summation in 0004afdc (pair 0x11efa/0x147ca gated by bit 6 of ffff41ab) and normalization (V * M) / 50000 in 0006205c, where V is output of 0x1495a, M is output of 0x1459a or 0x145ca, and 50000 is divisor literal 0xC350.
contract: Unsigned 32/32 division: r0 = r1 / r0 (dividend r1, divisor r0), rounding down. The implementation is an unrolled div0u/div1 sequence that selects a path by operand bit width. It does not return a remainder: on exit r1 contains an unreconstructed remainder mixed with quotient bits. r2 and r3 are preserved on the stack, and PR is untouched. On division by zero it writes 0x0000044E to 0xFFFF9818 and returns 0. Its pair 00021f40 returns the remainder under the same convention.

Unsigned 16/16 division: r0 = (r1 & 0xFFFF) / (r0 & 0xFFFF), with the result zero-extended to 32 bits. Wide inputs are silently truncated: divisor 0x10003 acts as 3. It clobbers r1 and preserves r2-r15. On division by zero it writes 0x0000044E to 0xFFFF9818 and returns 0.

Signed 32/32 remainder: r0 = r1 % r0 under the C rule, where the result has the sign of the dividend and is unaffected by the divisor sign; its magnitude is strictly less than the divisor magnitude. The quotient is computed and discarded. It clobbers r0 and r1; r2, r3, and r4 are preserved on the stack. On division by zero it writes 0x0000044E to 0xFFFF9818 and returns 0.

Unsigned 32/32 remainder: r0 = r1 % r0, strictly less than the divisor by construction. The quotient is computed and discarded. It clobbers r1. On division by zero it writes 0x0000044E to 0xFFFF9818 and returns 0. It is the canonical pair of 00021ce0: same convention and operands, remainder instead of quotient.

Not arithmetic: longword block copy. It copies r0 bytes from [r2] to [r1], with r0 divisible by 4. For r0 <= 0x40 it unrolls through jump table 0x22094; otherwise it loops. It returns no result and clobbers r0; r2 and r3 are preserved on the stack. It writes only destination range [r1, r1+r0) and has no diagnostic channel.

Not a function: a 17-longword jump table at 0x22094..0x220d7 belonging to the copier entered at 00022038. Ghidra declared it as a separate function by combining data with code. The copier convention is r0 = byte length, r1 = destination, r2 = source.

Not arithmetic: block copier, even-parity entry into unrolled ladder 0x22116. It copies r0 bytes from [r2] to [r1], with r0 divisible by 4 and an even count of 0..16 longwords; writes proceed in descending order. It returns no result and clobbers r0; r1 and r2 are preserved, with r3 preserved on the stack. The paired odd-parity entry is 00022104.

Not arithmetic: block copier, odd-parity entry into the same ladder 0x22116. It copies r0 bytes from [r2] to [r1], with r0 = 4 mod 8, or 1, 3, .. 15 longwords. The unrolled sequence alternates r0 and r3 as transfer registers, so parity selects the entry. Its paired entry is 000220f8.

Not a standalone function: internal point in the unrolled copy ladder, at the 16-longword step. Public entries are 000220f8 and 00022104; this address is statically unreachable because its only reference is the 0x40 entry in table 0x22158. Invalid length fails in hardware rather than silently: r0 not divisible by 4 or r0 > 0x40 sends the dispatcher beyond the table and causes an address error. At r0 = 0 no copy occurs, but a stray read from [r2-4] still happens.

Logical left shift: r0 = r0 << r1, with a signed count. For r1 < 0 it returns the input unchanged; for r1 >= 32 it returns 0. The shifted value is necessarily r0 because paths 28..31 use the encoding and #imm,r0 and cannot target another register. It clobbers r1; r2 is preserved on the stack. It does not write global RAM; memory accesses are the stack and a byte read from table 0x2219c. T is not a contractual output.

Not a standalone function: count-7 leaf of left-shift ladder 000221bc and also the base of its jump table. It computes r0 = r0 << 7, discarding bits beyond bit 31 without saturation. Entry is only through the dispatcher's jmp: rts restores r2 placed on the stack by prologue 000221bc, so a direct call would misalign the stack.

Logical unsigned right shift: r0 = r0 >> r1 with zero fill. A jump table dispatches into a chain of fixed shifts: SH-2E has no SHLD/SHAD, so variable shift is unrolled by count. It clobbers r1; r2 is preserved on the stack. It is pure, writes no memory, and has no diagnostic channel.

Not a standalone function: count-7 leaf of unsigned right-shift ladder 0002227c. It computes r0 = r0 >> 7 with zero fill. The leaf does not read count r1 because the dispatcher has already consumed it. Entry is only through the dispatcher's jmp: rts restores r2 placed on the stack by its prologue.

Not a function: data forming the tail of jump table 0x2231c..0x2235b, entries for counts 24..31, belonging to arithmetic right-shift dispatcher 0002235c. Ghidra declared the table tail as a separate function.

Arithmetic signed right shift: r0 = (int32)r0 >> r1, dispatched through a 32-entry jump table. The count is compared as signed. It clobbers r1; r2 is preserved on the stack. It is pure, with no RAM writes and no error branch.

Not a standalone function: count-24 leaf of arithmetic right-shift ladder 0002235c. It computes r0 = (int32)(int8)(r0 >> 24), sign-extending the high byte; the result is always in -128..127. Entry is only through the dispatcher's computed jmp.

semantics: Pure arithmetic-shift helper used by fuel, misfire, and diagnostic calculations.
contract: Arithmetic right shift by 7: r0 = (int32)r0 >> 7, equivalent to signed division by 128 rounded down toward negative infinity. The body is seven consecutive shar instructions followed by rts; the seventh shift occupies the return delay slot. It has no memory access and preserves PR and r1-r15. Side output is T = input bit 6.
note: FUN 00056fc0 passes a signed product directly, so negative values retain floor-rounding before its explicit lower clamp.

contract: Arithmetic right shift by 6: r0 = (int32)r0 >> 6, signed division by 64 rounded down. The body is six shar instructions and rts. It is pure, with no memory access, and does not touch the stack or PR. Side output is T = input bit 5.

Arithmetic right shift by 10: r0 = (int32)r0 >> 10, signed division by 1024 rounded down. The shlr8/swap.w/exts.b/xtrct sequence restores the sign because SH-2 has shlr8 but no shar8. It does not write RAM; its only memory access spills r1 to the stack. Side output is T = input bit 9.

Arithmetic right shift by 11: r0 = (int32)r0 >> 11, signed division by 2048 rounded down. It is pure; its only memory access spills r1 to the stack. Ghidra renders the return as CONCAT44(in_r1, ...), which is a decompiler artifact: r1 is not computed and is restored from the stack.

Arithmetic right shift by 12: r0 = (int32)r0 >> 12, signed division by 4096 rounded down. The result is within -524288..524287 for every input, so overflow is impossible. It is pure, has no RAM writes or error channel, and is total over its entire domain.
Arithmetic right shift by 13: r0 = (int32)r0 >> 13, signed division by 8192 rounded down. It is pure; its only memory access spills r1 to the stack. It has no branches or special cases.

Not arithmetic: bytewise block copy. It copies r0 bytes from [r2] to [r1] in ascending address order. The loop is unrolled by four bytes, but the bound is checked after every byte, so an arbitrary-length tail is copied exactly. It returns no result; r2, r3, and r4 are preserved on the stack. It writes only the destination block and touches no fixed RAM addresses.

semantics: Samples on-chip A/D channels AN10 and AN17 through FUN 0002df5c, shifts each aligned result right by six, and writes the resulting 10-bit values to ffff362c and ffff362e.
note: Downstream adjustment, paired accelerator-pedal diagnostics, and P2122/P2123/P2127/P2128 monitors establish that these two analog channels belong to the dual-channel accelerator-pedal path.

semantics: On-chip A/D single-conversion helper. The unsigned channel argument selects one of the SH7059 A/D result registers, starts a conversion, waits for completion, and returns the aligned unsigned 16-bit result.
note: The caller shifts the returned aligned register value right by six to obtain a 10-bit sample.

contract: Signed 32-bit absolute value: r0 = abs(r4). The argument is passed in r4 rather than r0 or r1, unlike the rest of the library convention. r4 also holds the result on exit because neg r4,r4 overwrites a negative argument. The body has five register instructions, no memory access, and one acyclic branch.

semantics: Signed comparator with an optional subtractive hysteresis offset. FUN 0004d2a6 uses it to maintain ffff24a9.bit6 from raw coolant snapshot ffff1071, ROM8[00008e00]=170, and offset 3.
contract: It returns uint8 1 iff int32(r4 - (uint8(r7) != 0 ? r6 : 0)) <= int32(r5); otherwise it returns 0. It reads and writes no memory.
note: With bit 6 clear, the caller sets it while ffff1071<=170. With bit 6 set, subtracting 3 retains it through ffff1071=173 and clears it at ffff1071>=174. The comparator contract is exact; the physical coolant conversion remains separate.

semantics: Diagnostic runtime-record result-state predicate. It addresses the three-byte record array at ffff5718 + 3*index and tests bits 5 and 6 of the third byte.
contract: Input r4 is interpreted as a signed 16-bit record index. Index -1 returns 0 without reading RAM. Every other index returns 1 when either bit 5 or bit 6 is set in byte 2 of ffff5718 + 3*index, and returns 0 when both bits are clear.
note: The record bits are kept as operational result-state bits; no UDS status names are assigned.

semantics: Composite diagnostic-record gate used by the P030 common readiness path. It returns nonzero when any checked runtime record has bit 5 or bit 6 set in its third byte.
contract: It returns 1 when FUN 000259e4 returns 1 for any index in {0x14, 0x47..0x4c, 0x8a..0x8c}; otherwise it returns 0. The two calls with index -1 are inert because FUN 000259e4(-1) always returns 0.
note: The exact record set is code-proven. Its physical grouping name remains unresolved.

semantics: Signed multiplication wrapper around 0x2657C for a negative multiplier; it reads no tables. One of four non-table entries in the region, with 6 slots.

Implicit-axis 2D entry outside both enumerated models: calls 0x26AE0 for each axis and passes the result to 2D finisher 0x26770 with row stride 8. The two 8x8 maps are 0xA8EA and 0x9EDA; inputs are byte[ffff106f] and byte[ffff10f0].
note: The region's 35th table entry is not recovered by the resolver; findings.csv declares both maps in the manual layer.

semantics: Explicit-axis 4x4 wrapper over the byte core; geometry is in the entry registry.

The only 2D entry without a finisher: it reads the point directly (RTS + MOV.B @R4,R0 in the delay slot), while fractional parts of both axes are computed and discarded. Row stride is pool constant 0x260F8 = 4 rather than an immediate.
note: The journal had listed the existence of a non-interpolating family as an open question. Three converging observations identify the element as unsigned: both callers truncate the result to a byte, the rest of the 2D family is unsigned, and both maps contain monotonic data.

semantics: Explicit-axis 4x4 wrapper over the byte core; geometry is in the entry registry.
Explicit-axis 8x8 wrapper over the byte core; geometry is in the entry registry.
Explicit-axis 8x8 wrapper over the byte core; geometry is in the entry registry.
Explicit-axis 16x16 wrapper over the byte core; geometry is in the entry registry. It obtains axes through GBR-relative references rather than a shared literal, so each map has its own axes.
note: Method note: the extractor must recover gbr+offset, not only pc-literal, or r5/r6 are lost.

semantics: Explicit-axis 16x16 wrapper over the byte core; geometry is in the entry registry.

Explicit-axis 16x16 wrapper over the byte core and the only entry using finisher 0x267CC. The finisher performs both interpolation stages on bits 0..6 and then copies bit 7 from the lower-left cell selected by the row and column searches. Maps are 0x991A/0x9A1A/0x9B1A.
note: Bit 7 is not numerically interpolated.

semantics: Explicit-axis 8x8 wrapper over the word core; geometry is in the entry registry.
Explicit-axis 16x16 wrapper over the word core, with both axes using words (clamps 30/30 through one r7 pointer).

Mixed 16x16 wrapper: r5 axis is byte-based through core 0x26A0C (clamp 15), while r6 axis is word-based through 0x26984 (clamp 30); shll doubles the byte-axis index to a word stride. One of two mixed wrappers in the catalog.
note: Element type belongs to the (wrapper, axis) pair rather than the core: the clamp establishes both axis length and element type.

semantics: Explicit-axis 16x16 wrapper over the byte core; its sole caller is accessor 00082c8a, making it a local wrapper. It is the only entry using finisher 0x268A4, which saturates the sample when element bit 7 is set.
note: The shared interpolation functions are the primitives reachable through PTR_FUN slots, not this wrapper.

semantics: Implicit-axis primitive: 4 points, step 64, limit 192, uint8 element. No axis array exists; arithmetic in the core chain defines the axis.
Implicit-axis primitive: 8 points, step 32, limit 224, uint8 element. The busiest bank entry has 61 slots and 90 tables.
note: All 107 sites set r5 in the delay slot, so backward-only backtracking would recover no inputs. A slot is not a call: FUN_0005185c has one slot at 0x5197c and performs six lookups through it.

semantics: Implicit-axis primitive: 16 points, step 16, limit 240, uint8 element. It has 31 slots and 57 tables.
Implicit-axis primitive: 32 points, step 8, limit 248, uint8 element.
Implicit-axis primitive: 4 points, step 16384, limit 0xC000, uint16 element.
Implicit-axis primitive: 8 points, step 8192, limit 0xE000, uint16 element.
Implicit-axis primitive: 16 points, step 4096, limit 0xF000, uint16 element.
Implicit-axis primitive: 64 points, step 256, limit 0x3F00, uint16 element.

Implicit-axis primitive: 16 points, step 16, limit 240. Its output differs from the bank: DAT_0002646C = 128 is subtracted from the result, so values use offset-binary with 128 as zero, forming a signed correction map.
Canonical explicit-axis wrapper: 1D-8 over the byte core, with a body and its own two-slot pool for core and finisher. The clamp in the delay slot sets point count, and row stride sets row width.
note: Wrapper geometry is readable from its code and does not require caller traces. The rule reproduces all five wrappers whose dimensions were previously established by independent traces.

semantics: Explicit-axis 1D-16 wrapper over the byte core; geometry is in the entry registry.
Explicit-axis 1D-8 wrapper over the word core; geometry is in the entry registry.
Explicit-axis 1D-16 wrapper over the word core; geometry is in the entry registry.

Explicit-axis 1D-32 wrapper over the word core. Both sides of reciprocal pair 0x15500/0x15690 use it: at 0x732A8 base 0x15500 uses axis 0x15690, while at 0x72E1E/0x7549A/0x7AAE0 their roles are reversed.
note: The site, not the array, determines base and axis roles: these are direct and inverse tables of one relationship.

semantics: Explicit-axis 1D-16 wrapper with a word axis and byte element: SHLR R4 converts the byte offset returned by the core back into an element index.

Pure signed fixed-point multiplication helper. It multiplies the absolute 32-bit first argument by the unsigned 16-bit second argument, shifts the 48-bit product according to the signed byte third argument, and restores the first argument's sign.
contract: For the fuel call (r4=v, r5=G, r6=-2), return trunc_toward_zero(int32(v)*uint16(G)/16384). The helper has no memory access; negative results are sign-restored after magnitude scaling.
note: The call-specific denominator follows from the helper's implicit 16-bit product alignment and two-bit left shift for r6=-2.

semantics: Saturating addition that returns INT_MIN/INT_MAX on overflow; reads no tables. One of four non-table entries in the region, with 11 slots.
Explicit-axis 8x8 wrapper over third word core 0x26B84; geometry is in the entry registry.
Explicit-axis 16x16 wrapper over core 0x26B84; geometry is in the entry registry.
Mixed 16x16 wrapper over core 0x26B84: r5 axis is byte-based through 0x26BC4 and r6 axis is word-based, with clamps 15 and 30. The second of two mixed wrappers in the catalog.
Implicit-axis primitive: 16 points, step 4096, limit 0xF000, uint16 element; its core is the second copy of shift chain 0x26C1C.
Explicit-axis 1D-8 wrapper over core 0x26B84; geometry is in the entry registry.
Explicit-axis 1D-16 wrapper over core 0x26B84; geometry is in the entry registry.

Explicit-axis 1D-32 wrapper over core 0x26B84. Wave 2 used it to recover reciprocal pairs in component 00072f1e, where each table is the other's axis; search proceeds downward and [+0x3e] is the upper bound.
note: Wave 2 prose calls it a core, while the entry registry classifies it as a wrapper over core 0x26B84. This is a naming difference, not a geometry difference.

semantics: 1D linear interpolation: if (y1 < y0) return y0 - ((y0-y1)*frac >> 16); return y0 + ((y1-y0)*frac >> 16). Branching avoids signed overflow on a descending segment. Registers are y0=R0, y1=R2, frac=R3.
contract: Unsigned linear interpolation between r0=y0 and r2=y1 at Q0.16 fraction r3 in 0..65535. On a descending segment it returns y0 - floor((y0-y1)*r3/65536); on an ascending segment it returns y0 + floor((y1-y0)*r3/65536). The result lies between y0 and y1. MACL is preserved through r1; r1 and r2 are clobbered, r3 and PR are preserved, and the stack is balanced.
note: This is a lower-level primitive rather than the bank core. Twelve functions hold pointers to it, so enumerating from it yields 230 sites instead of one; the registry declares wrapper 0x2642C for it.

semantics: 2D interpolation over bytes, plain uint8: the full byte is the value. It serves six explicit-axis entries plus 0x26040. Both operands of each interpolation are read unsigned with EXTU.B.

2D interpolation over 7 bits: element bit 7 is a pass-through flag. The low 7 bits are interpolated (AND R9,R2 with R9=0x7F); bit 7 comes from the base cell and is returned in the result (TST R1,R2; OR R1,R0 with R1=0x80). Its only entry is 0x26230.
2D interpolation over words; entries 0x26270, 0x262A8, and 0x262E0. Both operands are read unsigned with EXTU.W.

2D interpolation over bytes with saturation: each cell is checked against 128 with CMP/HS, and when element bit 7 is set the entire sample output becomes 128 through MOV R6,R0. Values are therefore 0..127. Its only entry is 0x26320.
note: This explains the shape of 0xB61A: 136 of its 256 cells equal 128 in one contiguous high-RPM, low-load region. They represent saturation, not values. The same arithmetic disproves the x-64 degrees scale.

semantics: Byte-axis interpolation core: searches downward for the first axis element <= key using ADD #-1,R4; sub-helper 0x26C78 computes the second-stage fractional part. Eleven wrappers serve 94 tables; wrapper geometry is recorded in defs/JK08A.interp.csv from the clamp.
note: One of three explicit-axis cores. The cores are byte-identical except for axis element width; downward-search stride is the decisive distinction.

semantics: Word-axis interpolation core: same body as 0x26944, with downward-search stride ADD #-2,R4. Seven wrappers serve 107 tables; sub-helper 0x26C78 computes the fractional part.
Byte-axis search called by mixed wrapper 0x262E0 for r5 when r6 is word-based.

Entry into implicit-axis shift chain 0x26A5C..0x26A94. The chain contains consecutive SHLR R5 / ROTCR R3 pairs; entry K pairs above the merge yields index = raw >> K, so step = 2^K. This is the core for primitive 0x263BC with step 16384.
note: 0x26A5C..0x26A88 are not seven functions but offset entries into one chain. Adjacent entries are 4 bytes apart, exactly one SHLR/ROTCR pair.

semantics: Offset entry into the same shift chain, core for primitive 0x263D8 with step 8192; it holds a pointer to 0x26740.
Per-axis implicit search for entry 0x26040. It is called once per axis, so the axes for this map pair are implicit as in the bank.
1D linear interpolation for entries using core 0x26B84; its formula is identical to 0x26740.
2D interpolation over words; entries 0x265F0, 0x26628, and 0x26660.
Third explicit-axis word core; six wrappers serve 22 tables. Sub-helper is 0x26BC0.
Byte-axis search called by mixed wrapper 0x26660 for r5 when r6 is word-based.
Second independent copy of the implicit-axis shift chain: 12 SHLR/ROTCR pairs, step 4096. Core for primitive 0x266A0.
Sub-helper for cores 0x26944 and 0x26984: the second search stage that computes the fractional part.
Finisher recovered by wave 2 in the crossfade blend path of component 0007a804 together with core 0x26B28.
Writes a RAM structure and reads no tables. One of four non-table entries in the region, with 3 slots.
Caller of init routine 0002c648.

Masked six-channel ATU-II one-shot scheduler. Its callers supply duration array ffff224e or ffff1568. For each set bit in the channel mask it selects a 16-bit duration; ffff22e0 and ffff1935 substitute injector opening time ffff23aa for that channel, and a DSTR start bit that is still set causes the same opening time to be subtracted from the new duration. It scales the selected value by 800/256 with uint16 saturation, optionally forces 1000 through ffff4251 bit 0, adds the result to ATU-II channel 8 down-counter DCNT8A..DCNT8F at fffff640..fffff64a with interrupts masked, and sets the corresponding start bit in DSTR at fffff666.
note: The SH7059 hardware manual identifies the addressed registers as ATU-II channel 8 one-shot pulse outputs. With PSCR1 = 1 from 000274ac and TCR8 = 0x55 from 0002718a the counters step at Pphi/64, so the 800/256 factor makes one duration count 200/Pphi = 10 us exactly. Pin-tracer injector-terminal mappings remain cross-model candidates, so physical injector identity is not asserted at code confidence.

semantics: Analog acquisition and coolant conversion path. It stores the 16-bit result of FUN 00028668(0) at ffff1d60, writes uint8(result >> 2) to ffff1186, converts that byte through calibration 00012dea into ffff1079, and calls FUN 00039634 to form normalized coolant index ffff1077. It acquires the fuel-temperature sample through FUN 00028668(0, 0xe000) into ffff100a at 0002c554, writes uint8(sample >> 2) to ffff1178, converts it through the same table into transfer code ffff1f89 and DID 0x1104 byte ffff1074 at 0002c56e, and calls FUN 000398b0. The function also acquires additional analog channels and applies flat correction map 00012d8a to peripheral word ffff5620.
note: Exact UDS DID 0x1101 returns ffff1079 and DID 0x1104 returns ffff1074. Both bytes are deg C+50, the code that the ECU declares for table 00012dea through J1979 Mode 01 PIDs 0x05 and 0x0F; the physical identity does not rely on the shape of the calibration.

semantics: Component whose map-read path is selected by ffff2451 and ffff4185. On the 00012332 path, lookup by uint8 ffff1077 writes the raw byte to ffff1f24 and its x<<8 representation to ffff1e54.
note: The physical roles of states ffff1f24 and ffff1e54 are unresolved; x<<8 is an internal representation rather than a map scale.

semantics: Init/reset routine that fills RAM with default values and initializes several calibration paths. For Base Fuel Schedule, it looks up M from uint16 fallback map 0x15630 by uint8[ffff1077]<<8, writes M to ffff1e44 and M>>2 to ffff1e40, and calculates q=min(65535,floor(M*uint8[ffff1160]/512)). It writes q to ffff1062, min(65535,4*q) to ffff1dee and ffff1e06, and, when ROM8[0x8d92].bit4 is set as in stock JK08A, to ffff1dec and ffff1e04. The same min(65535,4*q) initializes newest diagnostic word ffff1026. It also copies throttle-limiter scalar 0x942c to ffff1796 and forms selector ffff23ed from map 0x1218e.
note: The initialization arithmetic and ffff1026 sink are exact. The Base Fuel Schedule identity follows from the exact DID 0x1208 binding. The raw/2048 ms conversion of map 0x15630 remains candidate evidence pending hardware validation.

semantics: One-time read initializer: flat 0xFF maps 0x120be/0x12c3a, which are byte-identical, are read once under latch bit 2 of ffff24b8: tst 0x4 on entry and or 0x4 after the read.
note: The 0xFF contents cannot be resolved without tracing the calibration-layer write: they may be unprogrammed flash or a saturated limit.

semantics: Selector writer for ffff1e60: ffff4246 bit 6 clear selects ffff3a76, while bit 6 set selects ROM word 0x916c. FUN_0003b520 calculates ffff3a76 through a separate inverse-table branch, and 0003b498 reads ffff1e60.

Accessor for the electronic-throttle and airflow calculation subsystem, with 20 maps and 22 accessors. Its structural backbone consists of reciprocal 1D-32 pairs through wrapper 00026524: 00013202/000155a0 is the primary target-throttle angle/opening-area conversion, while 00015500/00015690 and 00015540/000156d0 form an unresolved piecewise conversion.
note: Code establishes the reciprocal topology and paired throttle-feedback use of 00013202/000155a0. Its physical Target Throttle Valve Opening identity and scales x*0.0008 cm^2 and x*0.0275 degrees remain catalog candidates. The other two reciprocal pairs remain physically unresolved. Maps 00014cea/00015082/00015062 are live unless a disabling branch is demonstrated.

semantics: Two independent calculations share one routine. The first converts outputs A=out(0x14274) and B=out(0x141F4) into contribution bytes wA=uint8(trunc0((A<<8)/(A+B))) and wB=uint8(trunc0((B<<8)/(A+B))), then partitions common value T=ffff2842 into ffff2844=(T*wA)>>8 and ffff2846=(T*wB)>>8. The second uses inverse pair 0x13202/0x155A0 and RAM inputs ffff284a/ffff284c to calculate ffff3a76; the paired-curve outputs do not feed this branch.
note: The full 456-byte exact-JK08A machine listing includes blocks 0003b5d0, 0003b60c, and 0003b630 omitted by the decompiler. Their signed-correction branches are unreachable for the unsigned, nonnegative operands used here.

semantics: Fuel-compensation coordinator. It retains the established 0x09CEA -> ffff1efc and 0x09E3A -> ffff115b paths, selects working word ffff115c, and on the active Fuel Compensation Main path looks up 0x0A29A through 000261f0 on axes 00011cf0/00011d4c before writing its uint8 result to ffff1160. Runtime gates can write a bounded bypass byte to the same destination.
note: The stock 0xA29A representation is Q7 with raw 128 neutral. ffff115c is a separate selected word and must not be identified as the 0xA29A result.

semantics: Component enabled by master gate bit 7 of ffff84c0. On the r5>=r7 branch, map 00012126 defines floor((r5-r7)*x/2048). Separately, lookup 00012332 by uint8 ffff1077 defines a lower raw bound: code selects max(lookup<<8,uint16[ffff1e5c]).
note: The physical purpose of both computed quantities is unresolved; shifting lookup 00012332 by 8 bits is an internal representation.

semantics: Paired-channel forward-average-inverse conversion through 00013202/000155a0. Bits 0/1 of ffff23a6 select two sources; each source is multiplied by four and converted through 00013202, the opening-area-domain results are averaged, and inverse lookup through 000155a0 returns a coordinate that is divided by four and written to ffff3f7c.
note: Code proves the transform. The physical throttle-angle/opening-area labels and engineering scales remain catalog candidates.

semantics: Dual-channel corrected conversion. FUN 0003ef74 forms adjusted coordinates Z1/Z2, which are saved to ffff322c/ffff322e. Let Y1/Y2 be lookups of common curve 000148fa at Z1/Z2, A1/A2 be lookups of 0000c10e/0000c18e, O1/O2 be signed ffff45a0/ffff45a2, and P1/P2 be signed ffff2b54/ffff2b56. The function writes clamp(Y1+A1+O1+P1-32768,0,65535) to ffff29e2 and the parallel second-channel result to ffff29e4.
note: Stock ROM16[00008ea4]=0, so P1/P2 cannot change either output. The vendor AFR Conversion Table name and the downstream two-bank fuel-trim context support a physical hypothesis but do not establish an engineering scale; code confidence is limited to the conversion and correction arithmetic.

semantics: Paired-curve normalization branch. Let q=min(2*uint8[ffff22e4],255), A=lookup_u8(00012798,q), B=lookup_u8(000127d8,q), A128=lookup_u8(00012798,128), and B128=lookup_u8(000127d8,128). When A>B and A128>B128, n=min(255,floor(256*(A-B)/(A128-B128))); otherwise n=0. With ffff2451.bit1 clear, correction=floor(n*lookup_u8(00012704)/8); with the bit set, correction=0. The branch writes sat_u16(floor((correction+256*uint8[ffff22e4])/4)) to ffff11f2.
note: The formulas and selector polarity are exact. The physical quantities of q, n, correction, and ffff11f2 remain unresolved.

semantics: Conditional normalization of the selected curve term. When ffff2465.bit6 or ffff2468.bit2 is set, D=u16(ffff1752)+4*u8(ffff1765)+u8(ffff1763)+u8(ffff1f62). For D!=0, the function writes clamp(floor(s16(ffff2266)*128/D)+128,0,255) to ffff2315; separate endpoint rules handle D=0. When both gates are clear, it writes 128.
note: The arithmetic and gate behavior are exact. The physical quantity represented by the normalized byte is unresolved.

semantics: State and corridor controller. On its calibration-read branch it looks up shared curve 000122d2 by uint16[ffff11f0] over axis 00014d2a and writes ffff2523; downstream code uses only whether this byte is zero. Separately, 00014caa defines an upper signed bound, 00014e92 defines a lower signed bound, and code selects max(lower,min(upper,value)) before writing ffff2260.
note: The 000122d2 result is a nonzero gate; its magnitude is not consumed in this function. Both corridor bounds decode as x-32768. The physical quantities and branch purposes remain unresolved.

semantics: Two-table calculation: 2D 8x8 uint16 map 0xD80E produces signed ffff1750, while coefficient 0x12964 supplies g and computes sat_s16(trunc0(ffff1750*g/100)) in ffff1712. The same quantity reaches ffff170a only under a triple enable condition.
note: Interpolated g is written to ffff1767 and multiplies signed ffff1750 without a reload; 00021bbc divides the product by 100 with truncation toward zero. Saturation applies to the derived int16. Every cell of 0x12964 equals 100, so the current multiplier is 1. The physical quantity is unresolved.

semantics: Curve-form and branch selector. Let x=uint8[ffff22e4]. ROM8[00008710].bit3 set selects explicit-axis lookup over 00012778; clear selects implicit lookup at q=min(2*x,255). ffff244f.bit1 clear selects curve A (000127a8 explicit or 00012798 implicit), while bit1 set selects curve B (000127e8 explicit or 000127d8 implicit). The function writes 4*lookup to uint16 ffff1752.
note: Stock ROM8[00008710]=0x7c has bit3 set, so the explicit maps are active in this function. The physical curve quantity is unresolved.

semantics: Floor curves for a target quantity: byte-identical 1D-16 pair 0x12908/0x12918 with shared hash 786c40a671b09d6c, selected by bit 3 of ffff4250 and written to ffff171a. Consumer 000474a4 establishes the floor role by taking max(uVar4, ffff171a<<3). Under bit 5 of ffff2458, the same component also contains a peak-hold and implicit map 0x12042.
note: The map's own scale is not derived: the consumer multiplies by <<3, but that does not establish the unit of the map itself. Section 6 conflict: the catalog's 1D-16 and A2L concepts (load-100pct, overrun-fuel-cut) conflict with the traced target-quantity floor role and cannot be resolved by voting.

semantics: Composite weighted calculation: map 0x12808 produces 2*x in ffff1754; the value is multiplied by the centered output of map 0x12A42, then after negative-product correction the result is divided by 64 with truncation toward zero.
note: The physical purpose of the weighted result is unresolved.

semantics: Saturating aggregate builder. It calculates S=u16(ffff1752)+4*u8(ffff1765)+u16(ffff1748)+s16(ffff1230)+u8(ffff15ac)+u8(ffff13f7)+s16(ffff170a). When ROM8[0000870c].bit7 is set, u8(ffff1f62) is also added. The result clamp(S,0,65535) is written to ffff173a.
note: The aggregate is consumed in the air/throttle target path, but the individual physical quantity represented by ffff1752 remains unresolved.

semantics: Compensation component with disable/fault latch bit 3 of ffff41d0: when set it writes neutral value 0x80 instead of lookup 0001233a. A separate lookup of 00012352 by uint8 ffff10f4 is written to ffff2fc1 and combines with ffff2fc0 in two subsequent products with fixed shifts and saturation.
note: Physical names for 0001233a, 00012352, and 00012dd2 are unresolved. The range of 00012352 and catalog matches are not used for physical identification.

semantics: Consumer of floor curves 0x12908/0x12918: takes max(uVar4, ffff171a<<3), establishing the lower-bound role for quantity ffff122a in an air/throttle target calculation with opening-area multipliers.

Opening-area base builder. It stores lookup 0x1465a indexed by ffff106f<<8 in ffff1e74, stores lookup 0x1469a indexed by engine-speed word ffff11bc in ffff12fc, saturates their sum into ffff12fa, and writes min(ffff12fa,ffff133e) to ffff1340.
note: The exact raw composition and actuator-target consumption are code-proven. The catalog ISC Opening Area identity and engineering scale remain candidate semantics.

semantics: Accelerator-pedal high-state comparator. It compares normalized dual-channel sample ffff266e with ROM16[00008fdc]=610 when previous-cycle state ffff246d bit 7 is clear and with ROM16[00008fde]=528 when that state is set. The result is written to current state ffff246a bit 7.
note: Scheduler 00020dfe copies ffff246a to ffff246d once per cycle, closing activation/release hysteresis. The input producer traces to A/D channels AN10 and AN17. Exact diagnostic bindings identify the paired analog subsystem as accelerator-pedal sensors; no engine-speed path reaches this comparison.

semantics: Periodic-table index-65 knock and high-detonation timing-state coordinator. It consumes and clears threshold-exceedance count ffff2142; maintains signed Q8 state ffff1258 with a +13 quiet step or -307*count event step on one branch; updates selector ffff2466.bit6; and independently looks up the low seven bits of 0x9A1A and 0x9B1A. When ffff2469.bit7 is clear and ffff2467.bit6 is set it writes ffff121a=int16(ffff1380+((high_octane-high_detonation)<<8)); alternate branches slew-limit another Q8 state. It publishes ffff22fa as signed division by 256 truncated toward zero for consumer 0004d99c.
note: The direct map-difference formula is conditional. Other branches can copy, force, filter, or zero state, and the selector has additional gates. The count is cleared before the end-of-FUN-00020dfe snapshot boundary.

semantics: Per-evaluator-channel accessor for Knock Slice Map 0x1108E: it selects one of six 16-element uint16 rows by one-based channel number, interpolates the row through 000264f8 using speed axis 0x15340, and stores the threshold at ffff2144 + 2*(channel-1) for evaluator 0004a238.
note: The six uint16 thresholds occupy ffff2144..ffff214f. The apparent base reference ffff2142 in an indexed-listing comment is two bytes below the first effective one-based write and is the independent event counter. ROM axis 0x15340 corresponds to 400..6400 RPM. Stock ROM8[00008b3d].bit3 is clear, so the selected channel comes from ffff11de rather than alternate ffff2143. Physical cylinder or sensor order is not established.

semantics: Per-evaluator-channel knock monitor. It refreshes the current channel threshold through 00049ffc, compares the calculated uint32 metric with the selected uint16 threshold, writes the current result to ffff24c2 bit 6, sets or clears the selected bit in ffff2150, and saturating-increments ffff2142 on an exceedance.
note: The counter saturates at 0xff. The six bitmap positions follow the function's one-based internal channel selector; physical cylinder or sensor order remains unverified. Threshold 0xffff is the uint16 upper bound and effectively prevents an exceedance.

semantics: Cold/hot timing-map selector. It writes active sample ffff160f and cold/high-octane reference sample ffff1610. Through coolant raw 106 both use 0x991A; from 107 through 131 the active sample blends 0x991A with the hot surface selected by ffff2466.bit6 while the reference blends 0x991A with 0x9A1A; above 131 the active sample uses selected 0x9A1A or 0x9B1A and the reference uses 0x9A1A. Wrapper 00026230 interpolates bits 0..6 and preserves bit 7 independently. A ffff2468.bit3 and ROM8[0x8b3d].bit1 gate substitutes column key 0xff for the relevant normalized-BFS lookup.
note: The outputs feed timing state, limits, and knock control before the engine-event command. Code does not establish any of the three tables as a direct final angle relative to TDC. The map coordinate is exact at raw*100/128 percent of the fixed BFS reference.

semantics: Composite three-factor accessor for maps 0x1211E, 0x1212E, and 0x09D2A. Their interpolated uint8 results are multiplied, shifted right by 14, capped at 255, and written to ffff14d9.
note: 0x1212E has code-level scale x/128; the physical purpose of the composite result is unresolved.

semantics: Signed timing-state accumulator with an exact source selector for ffff1511. Priority is stock-inert feature map 000121a6, warm DFCO-transition map 0001219e, state-3/bit-7 constant ROM8[000086a2], then default/post-transition map 00012196. Map results and the constant use x-128. Coolant-indexed corrections 00011f0a/00011f12/00011f1a/00011f22 contribute through ffff12db, two-bank surface 00009dba through ffff1514, and multiplier 000147ca through ffff1349. The final byte is clamp_s8(s8(ffff1514)+u8(ffff12db)+s8(ffff1511)+u8(ffff1512)+u8(ffff1349)-128) at ffff23ee.
note: Map 0001219e requires ffff244f.bit2 clear, warm latch ffff41de.bit5 set, upstream DFCO bit ffff2458.bit5 set, and nonzero 85-count timer ffff2590. Map 000121a6 additionally requires ROM8[0000870b].bit0 set and ffff2318 below 0x4000; both conditions are false in the stock lifecycle. Constant 0x9e or +30 counts requires ffff22ff=3 and ffff2458.bit7 set. All remaining cases select 00012196. A target-vehicle capture establishes one-for-one propagation from 00012196 to the final software timing coordinate during warm deceleration. Physical degree units remain unverified.

semantics: Component where bit 7 of ffff2464 bypasses interpolation.

Composite four-factor calculation. Tables 0x11E46, 0x11E56, and 0x11E5E produce three coefficients for base byte ffff1294; the product is normalized by 2^24, written to ffff22f8, and its zero/nonzero state controls bit 0 of ffff2473.
note: The physical purpose of the composite coefficient is unresolved. Scale x/256 is established for 0x11E56; normalization allocation across the other factors remains in their individual claims.

semantics: Bounded-ramp coordinator. It selects lower threshold L from 0x1243A or 0x1244A by ffff2466.bit6, reads live Q7 normalized-BFS byte ffff1048, and combines it with upper coordinate C=ROM8[0x11ECD]=128 and a branch-specific upper value H from 0x12462 or 0x12472. On the code-proven bit-clear branch it calculates clamp(H*(ffff1048-L)/(C-L),0,H) when L<C and selects zero otherwise.
note: The live load representation is exact at raw*100/128 percent of ROM16[00009534]. Address 00011ecd is the terminal cell of ignition normalized-BFS axis 00011ebe, so C is exactly the 100-percent reference point; this function reads only that terminal cell and does not interpolate the axis. The physical purpose of the ramp output remains unresolved.

semantics: Timing-state compositor with an embedded 8x8 multiplier lookup at 0x0C50E. semantics: Cam-coordinate deviation correction builder in the ignition-angle path. It evaluates response curve 000125ca three times and writes the bounded result to ffff1a7d.

The target coordinate is clamp_u8(ffff2326+ffff2327-192), while bank coordinates use the corresponding actual intake and exhaust bytes. Map 000124b2 and mode gates select the coefficient branch or neutral replacement. The final engineering interpretation as valve-overlap correction remains a physical candidate.

semantics: Engine-event timing-correction builder. Otherwise it interpolates uint16 map 0x147da by ffff237e, stores the raw value in ffff2000, scales coefficient ROM8[0x8a3c] or ROM8[0x8a3d] (both 100, selected by ffff2459.bit5) by that value over 100 into ffff1ff6, forms ffff1ff8=ffff2378+ffff11d6 (or a one-count slew toward ffff2378 with timer ffff25fc when ffff24c0.bit6 is set), and writes ffff12d6=clamp_s8(ffff1ff8+ffff2356-ffff1ff6); with ffff40e7 nonzero and ffff24c2.bit1 clear the sum is limited to min(ffff11d6+ffff2356, -ffff40e7).

semantics: Final internal timing-coordinate builder. It forms mode byte ffff5b31 with hysteresis from coolant ffff1079 against raw 110, RPM/25 byte ffff11b3 against ROM8[0x8897]=48 and ROM8[0x8896]=128, and load ffff1048 against ROM8[0x8768]=64 and ROM8[0x8767]=96; writes ffff11da=clamp(ffff12d6+ffff564c, ROM8[0x8221]=-7, ROM8[0x821e]=50) with the ffff564c term included only while bits 1..5 of ffff5b31 are clear; optionally adds clamp(ffff9926,-10,0) under ffff99c4.bit2; rate-limits the sum against the previous ffff11d4 by at most ROM8[0x828a..0x828e]=4 counts upward per pass (ROM8[0x828f]=15 or ROM8[0x8291]=15 in the flagged modes) and ROM8[0x8291]=15 downward; re-clamps to -7..50; bounds it below by -(129-ffff1079) while coolant raw is below 130 and above by ROM8[0x83d5]-40=70; applies the override modes of ROM8[0x8b34], ROM8[0x8b42], and ROM8[0x86f9]; initializes to ROM8[0x8289]=0 on the first pass; and writes ffff11d4.

semantics: Primary APC command builder and diagnostic publisher. Normal branches calculate command=uint8(ROM8[0x83d5]-uint8(ffff11d4)), write it to ffff2022, and call 0002a892. semantics: Periodic-table index-27 six-channel fuel-output inhibit coordinator. semantics: Engine-speed fuel-cut state machine. Stock ROM8[00008b38] bit 7 is clear, so ffff2468 bit 4 selects one activation/release pair from the 2x2 uint16 table at 0000934e. With state ffff2497 bit 2 clear, RPM/12.5 word ffff11bc at or above the activation threshold inclusively arms bit 1 and loads optional delay ffff24f1; stock delay zero sets bit 2 in the same invocation. With bit 2 set, equality to the release threshold retains cut and only speed below it clears bits 1 and 2. The function returns bit 2 as a Boolean.

semantics: Stationary rev-limiter state machine in the aggregate fuel-output inhibit path. Entry requires coarse vehicle speed ffff110e == 0, ffff244f bit 2 set, and ffff2458 bit 5 clear. It loads ffff258a with 100; each expiry looks up 000124d2 at q=clamp((signed16(ffff11bc)-160)/2,0,255), adds lookup-128 to readiness accumulator ffff16a6 with saturation, and reloads the timer. Readiness bit 4 is set at accumulator >= ROM16[0000911c]. With readiness set, RPM/50 byte ffff11ae at or above ROM8[000085d9] sets fuel-cut bit 5; equality to ROM8[000085da] retains it and only a lower value clears it.
note: At or below 2000 RPM the stock step is zero. In the high-RPM limiter region it is 127, so three timer expiries reach the inclusive threshold 381. This is 300 tenth-phase counts, or 3.072 seconds at the target-measured 10.24 ms period. Returned bit 5 becomes global mask 0x3f.

semantics: Boolean-to-six-channel-mask helper: returns 0 when its input is zero and 0x3f when its input is nonzero.

BFS-threshold hysteresis contributor for ffff249f.bit0. It compares the high byte of ffff1024 with RPM-indexed 0-to-1 map 00012116 and 1-to-0 map 00012984; ffff25b9 additionally gates the transition to one.

semantics: Edge-sensitive DFCO cut-request evaluator. It always interpolates coolant-indexed RPM thresholds 000126e4 and 00012718 by ffff106f. With current ffff2458.bit5 clear it returns 0. A rising edge with previous ffff245a.bit5 clear requires coarse vehicle speed at least 4 and selects 00012718; a held edge selects 000126e4 on the common stock branch. It returns 1 only when RPM/25 ffff11b3 is strictly above the adjusted selected threshold.

Additional branches apply saturating offsets, lower bounds, and runtime gates. A true cut request is necessary but not sufficient for state-machine entry: FUN 000503e0 also requires restore class 0. The target-vehicle restore-only A/B result confirms that distinction in warm moving operation.

semantics: DFCO restore classifier. It always interpolates upper/intermediate threshold 0001298c and lower/full-restore threshold 00012818 by coolant index ffff106f, applies an RPM-drop-class-dependent floor and runtime floors, stores adjusted values in ffff1778 and ffff16aa, and compares them with RPM/25 ffff11b3. Return 0 permits or maintains cut, 1 is master inhibit or absent upstream mode, 2 is intermediate restore, and 3 is full restore.

The classes select RPM/25 floors 36, 48, 54, and 62, equal to 900, 1200, 1350, and 1550 RPM. Below coarse vehicle speed 4 the exact classification is RPM<=lower -> 3, lower<RPM<=upper -> 2, and RPM>upper -> 0. At speed 4 or above, every branch reachable with stock ROM8[00008b3f].bit7=0 and ROM8[0000870c].bit7=0 ignores the upper threshold and returns class 3 at or below the effective lower threshold, then class 0 only strictly above it. A warm moving target-vehicle capture changes the restore pair while retaining stock cut-request thresholds; because all selected samples use this moving branch, the elimination of full inhibit isolates 00012818 as the operational veto. Table 0001298c remains live only for the low-speed intermediate band under stock flags.

semantics: Mode-dependent accessor for a shared pool. With ROM[00008d92]=0x7a and bit 3 set, control transfers from 00051718 to 000517a8 and skips lookups of maps 00012206 and 000121f6 together with their downstream calculations. The executing branch uses 000121e6/000121ae/000121ce as cascaded multipliers.

semantics: Throttle-release detector and six-table calculation accessor; holds a pointer to 00026370 in slot 0005197c. Map 000121ae forms shared multiplier g=max(0,8192+(lookup-64)*uint8[ffff10bf]). Maps 0001220e and 000121d6 form ffff1534 and ffff1535. Map 000121fe is independently multiplied by g, normalized by 8192, saturated to 255, and written to ffff1531. Maps 000121c6 and conditionally updated 000121de combine with ffff1531 in a product normalized by 16384 for ffff1532. The detector is signed16[ffff10b8] < -ROM8[000086ae] and writes bit 0x10 of ffff24d2.

semantics: Mode-dependent six-channel calculation. ROM8[00008d92] bit 3 controls entry. When bit 3 is clear, the function runs an internal six-channel loop, evaluates a compound condition that includes current sample ffff1024 minus previous sample ffff1028 being greater than or equal to ROM8[000087fd]<<3, writes ffff1220, and uses map 000121ee in derived array calculations. The compound ffff1220 writer, the 000087fd comparison, and map 000121ee path do not execute in stock bit-3 mode and are not evidence for stock Over Run Fuel Cut. The derived 16-bit output is an injection duration in 10 us counts: FUN 00051f1e passes array ffff1568 to ATU-II one-shot scheduler 0002c13c.

When ffff1220 is nonzero, the function calls FUN 0002c13c with ffff1220 as the channel mask and the six-word duration array at ffff1568, then ORs the same mask into status bytes ffff14c3 and ffff14c2.

For the supplied channel bit, it sets the bit only when the corresponding ffff22e0 bit is clear, signed16[ffff142e+2*i] is greater than or equal to ROM8[000087fe]<<7, and the corresponding ffff16ff bit is clear; otherwise it clears the ffff1220 bit. ROM8[000087fe]=5, so the signed-difference threshold is 640 raw counts.

Stock value 0x7a selects the branch at 00052484: shared calculations call FUN 0005185c and FUN 00051700, then each of six channels passes through FUN 0005727a, FUN 00052034, and FUN 00051a98 among other calculations; after the loop, FUN 00051f1e schedules the selected channels. In this stock branch FUN 00052034, not FUN 00051a98, writes ffff1220.

semantics: Per-channel signed-difference producer used by the stock dispatcher. It scales either ffff1024 or ffff123e by ffff22e6, stores the current six-channel value, conditionally updates a held prior value, calculates current minus held, clamps the signed result to -32768..32767, and writes it to ffff142e+2*i. semantics: Composite accessor: 8x8 map 0000a8ea is read through 00026040 using implicit inputs ffff106f/ffff10f0, while uint16 map 00014ed2 is read through 000263d8 using saturated index 32*u16[ffff1222]. The output of 00014ed2 is multiplied by the uint8 output of 0000a8ea, normalized by >>7, saturated at 0xffff, and written to ffff1652.

Centered shaping curve 0001242a forms a second multiplier; after /64 normalization and saturation, the result is written to ffff15de.

semantics: Component enabled by a triple condition on ffff2481, ffff2458, and ffff249d. Map 0x1215E forms subtractive correction ffff14fc; 0004e614 passes it through an arithmetic right shift by 7 before subsequent weighted composition.
note: The physical purpose of the correction is unresolved.

semantics: Accessor for 4x4 family 0000a49a/0000ab6a through 00026084 and two 1D-8 upper bounds 000126b0/000126b8. The 1D lookups form a minimum; the selected value enters with weight ffff165b into (ffff165a*ROM8[0000886e]+ffff165b*min)/256, saturated at 255 and written to ffff15df. It uses current BFS ffff1024, looks up maps 0x129E2/0x129F2 into ffff17ba/ffff17bb, saturates their byte sum at 255, and applies complement multiplier (256-sum). Its terminal calculation writes ffff165e=floor(uint8(ffff160d)*ROM16[0x9332]/256), with ROM16[0x9332]=13972.

semantics: Composite accumulator: lookup 00012562 by uint8 ffff106f is successively multiplied by Q6 coefficients 00012572 and 00012582 with /64 normalization and by uint8 ffff10bf; a conditional branch can clear this first term. A separate 4x4 map 0000a49a supplies a multiplier for an additional term that also uses bytes ffff1600 and ffff1b14 plus ROM8[000087e8]. The saturated sum forms ffff230c, which participates in calculations of ffff231a and ffff18e2.

Coordinator 00057608 calls 00055098 before 00054ee0, so the latter reads the current selected 00012ede/bypass factor from ffff1b14. The physical quantity of the composite results is unresolved.

When ffff246b.bit6 is set, it interpolates map 00012ede on axis 00011bfb by min(u8[ffff2442],u8[ffff2443]); otherwise it substitutes raw 64. The shared >>12 does not assign an absolute fixed-point scale to all four factors or physical units to ffff15ce. VQ35HR JK00D homolog FUN 00056fc8 preserves the same 312-byte control and arithmetic structure with map 0001528b, axis 00013eb8, and a different gate bit. The physical subsystem remains unresolved.

note: The physical purpose of threshold ffff15cc is unresolved.

semantics: Commanded-mixture stage of coordinator 00057608 and sole stock runtime writer of ffff22e8. It looks up target mixture map 0000a9aa on engine-speed word ffff11bc and load ffff102c, with 0xff forced onto the load axis while wide-open latch ffff2468 bit 3 holds (the latch compares throttle-opening byte ffff3528 with the flat 200 of 0001214e on ffff11b3), scales the deviation from 128 by 00012552 on ffff11ae when ffff2466 bit 6 selects the high-detonation surface, applies enrichment latch ffff24a2 bit 7 (ROM8[00008b9b] = 130 on, ROM8[00008b9f] = 129 hold), and writes target byte ffff15eb. Composite accessor: uint8 output of map 0x11F2A multiplies ((uint16[ffff160a] * uint16[ffff165e]) >> 8), the product passes through logical right shift by 15 in 0002227c, and the resulting coefficient scales adjacent lookup results.

semantics: Component with three control bits and two calculation variants for ffff192e. Bit 4 of ffff2484 selects special lookup 0001230a with formula 2*min(y,209); normal branch 00012302 forms 2*min(y+uint8[ffff340c],209). Bit 1 of ffff41d0 latches disable/fault, bit 1 of ffff24d0 selects a bypass path, and 00012c12 is compared with difference uint8[ffff1071]-uint8[ffff106e].

semantics: Component where ffff24a0 is a mode selector and override.

Paired accessor for 0x14FD2/0x14FE2. Value 0x14FD2 is limited to 10..5000 and its low byte is written to ffff8b18. Value 0x14FE2 independently participates in two local comparisons and is stored in a stack slot after bound selection.

semantics: Shared interpolator for three components (0005fdb0, 000602f2, and 000617ea). Its body lies outside their boundaries, so the physical quantity of their argument cannot be resolved internally.

Dual-channel interpolator with two distinct offset-binary branches: 0x14C9A is indexed by axis 0x15D60 in nonnegative branches and forms ffff8c08/ffff8c0a; 0x14CBA is indexed by axis 0x15D70 in negative branches and forms ffff8c04/ffff8c06 after multiplication and limiting.

Each uint16 M is multiplied by a separate Q7 coefficient, after which the product is saturated or divided by 128.

semantics: Composite accessor for internal multipliers. Maps 0x1453A and 0x1454A form min(0xffff, floor(M*Q/64)). When initial states are zero, 0x15002 forms 255*M and derived min(255, floor((255*M)/20000)), while 0x15012 forms initial uint16 M through an exact multiplication and division pair with divisor 1071.

semantics: Raw-state and paired-output coordinator. Maps 0x13182, 0x131a2, 0x131c2, and 0x133d2 maintain Q12 accumulator ffff33a8; 0x1459a and 0x145ca form a normalized lower bound for ffff33a4 through coefficient 0x1495a; 0x14de2 and 0x14e02 provide a mode-gated output pair.

semantics: Component where ffff2465 and ffff24c2 select the source of a calibrated limit.

Multimode accessor for maps 0x0B5FA and 0x11FE6. Interpolated uint8 M from the selected map is multiplied by uint8 ffff3373; the product is written to ffff13dc and used as a zero-saturating decrement step for uint16 ffff1866.

It decodes transition readiness into ffff4253.bit6 and sets ffff4252.bit1 exactly when ffff418f.bit4 is set, current gear index ffff1082 differs from target gear index ffff1083, and bit 6 is clear. It sets ffff41a6.bit3 when bit 1 is set or retained byte ffff4413 is nonzero, and clears bit 3 otherwise.
